LESSON: GRAPHIC DESIGN

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: FINE ARTS
Strand: Multimedia Arts (2D Art)
Topic 2.2: Graphic Design
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Graphic Design, part of Multimedia Arts (2D Art) in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 FINE ARTS.

Key inquiry question: Why are graphic illustrations incorporated in a work of Art?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Graphic Design together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to learn: as the learner effectively research on elements of graphic design

● Imagination and Creativity: as the learner design a poster with a trade mark incorporated using computer aided

design

● Digital literacy: as the learner manipulates digital tools to design letters and write words.

Values:
● Social justice: as the learner acquires an understanding of equity and fairness in relation to gender while

creating a poster.

● Patriotism: as the learner writes messages inspired by civic education.

● Love: as the learner shares findings on elements of graphic design.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

● Financial literacy: as the learner conducts digital research to appreciate aspects of a trademark

● Health and promotional issues: as the learner creates a poster in freehand inspired by gender based issues.
